summary: Five canonical testament cases were reread from every supplied original page. William-lanark-1673 is a duplicate alias of william-1673, not a sixth case. The strongest direct family evidence is Bessie Glasgow as the 1650 John's sister and Agnes Watson plus the three lawful sons of the 1662 Leith maltman. The genuinely new correction is Alexander Broun, not George Broun, as William Glasgow's 1673 co-executor. Thomas Glasgow in the 1662 John entry remains a named administrator-context participant without proved sonship. Jonet [Kinnie?] remains the probable widow's name in 1685.

1662 John: death month, Thomas Glasgow's descriptor/exact capacity, account names, and any kinship
1662 Archibald: servant surnames, remaining account names/sums, exact will day, Thomas/William Glasgow kinship, and the maltman-versus-shoemaker identity seam

connections: 1650 directly proves John Glasgow and Bessie Glasgow were siblings at Quothquan.
1662 Archibald directly proves a Leith maltman household: wife Agnes Watson and lawful sons Archibald, George, and William Glasgow.
The 1662 maltman may be associated with Glasgow-3078, but the testament does not bridge him to the independently documented Leith shoemaker; keep the occupation conflict visible.
The 1662 John names Thomas Glasgow in an administrative context but does not prove Thomas was his son.
The 1673 record supplies administrators Alexander Brown and John Neilson and cautioner William Neilson, not relatives of William Glasgow on the visible wording.
The 1685 record proves Jonet was John's widow; William Wilkie, John Wyllie, and William Watson are officials/surety, not kin.
The 1650, 1661/1662, and 1685 Johns are three separate record-defined Quothquan people until a separate source proves identity or descent.
